findings.text: The task folder has no `requirements.md`: the owner's asks behind this diff (phantom "Thank you." reaching the chat, the stray "undefined" reply, the Whisper flags) exist only as truncated spawn titles in `session.jsonl` and in the minions' own folders under `session-f5eadae9/`. A fresh agent can't tell from this folder what was asked or whether it was met. Write the brief, with the owner's words linked, and list the three minion tasks (`minion-minion-phantom-gate`, `minion-minion-undefined-guard`, and the whisper flags) and their commits.

`Servex/Servex.js:507-509` says the new `-mc 0 --suppress-nst` flags take effect after "a Servex restart", but whisper is detached and a restart *adopts* the running process with its old args (`Servex/Process.js:352`, `adopt()`). So the flags never apply until whisper-server itself is stopped and started again. Fix the comment and the minion's landing note to say "stop and start whisper" (`stop_server`/`start_server whisper`), and do that once so the change is actually live.

`ux/Dictate/chat.js:97-104`: `last_final_info` is never cleared after `deliver()` reads it. So a later spoken sentence that has no Whisper final of its own (the browser engine, or `ComposerMic`'s path if it doesn't fire `panel.dictate.on_whisper`) is judged on an old clip's duration and word probability. The blast radius is small (blocklist phrases only, as `doc/phantom-gate.md` says), but resetting it to `null` after each use is one line.

`ux/Dictate/chat.js:99-103` wraps `panel.dictate.on_whisper` by reassigning it. If anything assigns `on_whisper` again later (VoiceStrip wires its own at `VoiceStrip.js:38`), the gate silently loses its info and falls back to the echo-active branch only. A listener/event would be sturdier, but this works today.

A real, deliberate spoken "Thank you." said while Recite is reading, or within 1.5 s after it stops (`echo_active()`), is dropped by design (`phantom-gate.js:190`). Nothing on screen says so: the drop happens before `DictateHealth.set` and is only a line in `ai/whisper/bucket.jsonl`. That's acceptable, but `doc/phantom-gate.md` should name this trade-off under "Known gap".

`ux/Dictate/test/phantom-gate.mjs:235` keeps its own copy of the phrase list rather than the real `BargeIn.PHANTOM_PHRASES`. The reason is stated (BargeIn.js is browser-only), but the test can't catch a mismatch with the real `noise()`. For example, the real one doesn't trim, so a `" Thank you."` with a leading space slips through both gates.
The `is_filler` doc comment at `Servex/agents/Sessions.js:1724` still lists only `(listening)`, punctuation and filler lines, not the new `undefined`/`null` case at line 1726.

`core/Plugin/Plugin.js:125` now tracks every instance, because the old `tracks` guard (only plugins with their own `detach`) is gone. Then `enable()` at `Plugin.js:133` runs `attach` again on all of them. A plugin with no real `detach` (a plain function, or the default no-op `Plugin.detach` at :173) is never detached by `unuse()`, so `use()` → `unuse()` → `use()` attaches it twice to the same instance, which doubles its listeners.

A per-instance override doesn't survive a class-wide toggle. `disable()` (`Plugin.js:141`) detaches an instance whose row says `enabled: true`, and `enable()` (:133) re-attaches an instance whose row says `enabled: false`, so the row stops matching what is attached. The test even writes this down as expected: `Plugin.test.mjs`, "its own explicit true no longer follows the class row once off". Skip instances whose `_plugins` row has its own `enabled` set, or reset the row when this happens.

`Recite.on_read` has no caller. `grep on_read` on qf-1 finds only `Recite.js`, and `ux/Dictate/chat.js` never sets it. Yet `ux/Dictate/doc/echo-and-turn-taking.md` ("Built: … `Recite.on_read` — all below are now live") and `audio/Recite/readme.md` ("`on_read` — have landed") say it works. So the assistant is never told where it was cut off. Either wire it (the `say` with `kind: "read"`, plus Servex's `(cut off after "…")` line), or change both docs to say only the hook exists.

The "one second of silence" rule isn't built, but the Recite readme says "the always-on 1 s hold … have landed". `Recite.start_or_hold()` (`Recite.js:161`) only checks `speaking()` at that moment. If the owner stopped 50 ms ago, or speaks quietly under the threshold, the reply starts at once. The comment above it ("at least 1 s of quiet") describes code that doesn't exist. The doc's proposal was "minimum 1 s, whatever the ear setting".

`cancel_unheard()` was inserted between `take()` and its doc comment (`Recite.js:485-487`). Now `cancel_unheard` carries two doc comments, the first one describing `take()`, and `take()` has none. Move the "Queue the finished sentences…" comment back down to `take()`.

`Plugin#plugins` (`Plugin.js:28`) builds the instance rows once, from `records`, on first read. A plugin `use()`d on the class after that never gets an instance row: `record()` at :108 adds only the class row.

findings.text: `Recite.cancel_unheard()` (`audio/Recite/Recite.js:513`) loops over `chunks` from index 0. `chunks` keeps every reply already played until a full `stop()` (`audio/Recite/readme.md:75`), so one cut reports every earlier, fully heard reply as "skipped". Each of those reaches the assistant as a false "(a reply was skipped, never heard…)" note (`ext/Chat/v2/report.js` `read()` → `Sessions.js:1111` → `notes.smart`). Start the skipped loop after `this.at` (and the cut reply's group), and add a test with one reply played to the end before the cut.

Review finding 2 is only half fixed. `Plugin.detach_instance()` (`core/Plugin/Plugin.js:137`) treats the inherited no-op `Plugin.detach` (:209) as a real undo: it clears `rec.attached` and runs nothing. So a plugin that is a `Plugin` subclass with no `detach` of its own still gets attached twice across `use()` → `unuse()` → `use()`. The old code excluded `p.detach !== Plugin.detach`; bring that check back here. The H16 test only covers a plain object with no `detach` at all.

`core/Plugin/doc/design-notes.md:16` still says "Live instances are tracked (WeakRef) only for a plugin that defines its own `detach`, so a plugin with no undo costs nothing per instance." Now every attached instance is tracked (`attach_instance` adds to `rec.live` and `rec.attached`), so the line is wrong and the 1e6-instance cost figure above it is out of date. Re-measure, or say it is no longer measured.

`ux/Dictate/doc/echo-and-turn-taking.md` adds a "Built" line, but the paragraphs under it still describe the old code as today's code. "Interrupts today… Proposed", "The start grace (not coded today)", "One second of silence… Proposed" and "It also gates… Both need the ear toggle on (`barge.on`); with it off a reply plays at once" are all stale now. "Telling the assistant where it was cut off" describes a `say` with `kind: "read"` and Servex erasing the unread rest, but what was built is a `context` note through `report.read()`, and nothing is erased. Rewrite these as built, and keep the unbuilt parts (the Servex-side erase, the in-flight `speak:false`) as open items.

`ux/Dictate/doc/settings-plugins.md` ("Known gap: core/Plugin's on/off is class-wide", and build order step 1) says another minion is adding per-instance rows and the panel should wait. This same diff builds those rows (`inst.plugins`, `toggle_plugin`), so replace the section with a pointer to `core/Plugin/readme.md` ("`inst.plugins`").

The brief behind this diff is `requirements-qf1.md`, and it is untracked (`git status`: `??`), as are `page.js` and `past-work.md`. The task folder has no `requirements.md`, the file this review was told to read. It is also stale: it says findings 2, 3 and 8 are "being fixed by another minion", and `ccbbbb573` fixed them. It also says asks 1–3 and 5–7 have "no plan or task id recorded in this folder", but `session.jsonl` now holds tasks `p7p1ixrp`, `l2ccgdxy`, `dpsp54uf`, `pgwjbatr`, `abt7o4r0`, `t9w15ewb`, `j4aatgso` and `skixe7xs`. Commit the folder, refresh those two lines, and link the task ids, so a fresh agent can continue from here.

Review finding 10 is still open. `Servex/agents/roles/mastermind.md:13` says even a 5–10 second job goes to a minion, while `Servex/agents/roles/vscode-mastermind.md:14` says "A 5–10 second job is cheaper to do than to delegate". One line in either file saying which seat each rule is for would settle it.

The class-holds-state question: `inst.plugins` is new per-instance state, but the `core/Plugin` page (`core/Plugin/page.js:66`) draws only `Badge.plugins`, the class rows. No page shows an instance's own rows or overrides. Add one demo instance with its own switch.

`Plugin#plugins` (`Plugin.js:35`) builds an instance's rows from `this.constructor.records` only, which holds the class's own plugins. A plugin used on a parent class does attach (`"new"` walks the chain), but it gets no row on a subclass instance, so it can't be switched per instance. `Host._plugin_instances` (:34) is also never swept of dead `WeakRef`s.

An instance switch-off of a plugin with no `detach` (`toggle_plugin(rec, false)` → `detach_instance` returns early) still writes `enabled: false` on the row (`PluginEntry.js:43`), while the plugin stays attached. The row then shows something that isn't true.

`Recite.heard_words()` (`Recite.js:795`) returns the first six words of the cut sentence. `read_note()` then tells the assistant it was "cut off after" those words, which is usually earlier than where the audio really stopped. The readme notes it's an estimate, but the note the assistant gets doesn't say so ("about", or "in the sentence starting…").

`settings-plugins.md`'s table describes `turn_wait_ms` as "No-flood (hold updates)… hold back-to-back replies", but it is the quiet a fresh reply waits for (`update_hold_ms` is the no-flood hold). Its last paragraph says "Five features… no switch at all" and then names two.

One "he" about the owner is left in a test message: `audio/Recite/Recite.test.mjs:349` ("the instant he speaks"). The `echo-and-turn-taking.md` paragraph still calls `"-"` "the sanctioned way out", which qf-9's brief rewrite drops, so it goes stale once both branches merge.

`Recite.cancel_unheard()` still reports a reply you already heard in full as "skipped" when the cut lands during a turn-taking hold. `finish()` (`audio/Recite/Recite.js:254`) leaves `this.at` on the last chunk that played, and `start_or_hold(i)` sets only `wait_at = i`. So in the hold, `was_going` is false and the "skipped" loop runs from that old `this.at`. Start the loop at `wait_at` when nothing is playing, and add the held case to the "does not report a reply already played to the end" test (`Recite.test.mjs:109`), which covers only the playing case.

The task folder has no `requirements.md`. The brief this review was pointed at does not exist. Only `requirements-qf1.md` (a map from commits to asks) and the 120-character title in `session.jsonl` say what the mastermind was asked to do. Without a `requirements.md` and a `plan.md`, a fresh agent cannot pick up the session's own brief (the six open tasks are listed, but not the original "study the voice system" ask in full).

The `Servex/agents/roles/mastermind.md:13` rewrite changes how EVERY mastermind works: "brief a minion to do it, even a 5–10 second job". No owner ask in this folder covers it. `requirements-qf1.md` item 1 credits it to owner-feedback ask 4, but ask 4 is about trimming the cue tags. The new rule also reverses the owner's 2026-10-03 rule ("a 5–10 second job is yours"), and the bullet now contradicts itself: it says don't delegate for expertise a skill can carry, then says brief a minion for a page. Cite the owner's words for the change, or narrow it to `mastermind-voice-system` alone (where `single-voice-assistant.md` already says it).

`ux/Dictate/doc/settings-plugins.md` ("Reachable by the item tool" and build-order step 3) says `POST /api/session/settings` still has to be extended to carry plugin config. On michael/dev it already does: `Servex/agents/Sessions.js:396` stores `s.plugins`, and `plugin_defaults()` (:404) is "Make default". The `mastermind-chat-settings` merge (7d32afd51) built that. As soon as qf-1 lands, the doc is stale, and it is a second design for something chat-settings owns (the owner-feedback "Overlap" bullet). Point it at chat-settings' doc instead.

`core/Plugin/doc/design-notes.md:16` now reads "Stale as of `ccbbbb573`…", which is history in a doc. Rewrite the line as current fact ("every attached instance is tracked; the cost measured above predates that"), or re-measure.

`Plugin#plugins` (`core/Plugin/Plugin.js`, the `get plugins()` getter) adds a WeakRef to `Host._plugin_instances` for each instance that reads its list, and nothing ever prunes that set. `rec.live` now tracks every attached instance, not only ones whose plugin has a `detach`. Both grow slowly, but they grow without bound on a long-lived page.

Show the class and its live instances: the new `inst.plugins` rows have no page that lists one instance's own rows. This is previous-round finding 8, recorded as still open in `requirements-qf1.md`. No live instance on today's pages uses it yet, so it stays a note.

`Recite.resume_after_cut` is the one new user-facing switch, and it is console-only (`audio/Recite/readme.md`, cutting-in settings). It is missing from the `settings-plugins.md` table that chat-settings will build the panel from. One row there would keep it from being lost.

`Servex/agents/single-voice-assistant.md:23` adds a new claim, not a trim: "`mastermind-voice-system` is hands-free the same way: it never reads or builds either… so it too answers fast". No role or brief for `mastermind-voice-system` says this, and `0153ff6b9` reverted the matching `mastermind.md` line because "no owner ask covers changing every mastermind". The same reasoning applies here. Either drop the sentence, or back it with that agent's own brief, so the voice seat isn't promised a speed nobody enforces.

`requirements-qf1.md` item 1 says `a328ad385` delivered "the bare `(pause)` cue". This diff never touches `Servex/agents/Sessions.js`, and the bare cue (`Sessions.js:763`) is already on `michael/dev`. So the qf-1 commit only trims the brief's bullets (`single-voice-assistant.md:14-18`). Correct the attribution.

The "one second" hold is really 2.5 s by default. `Recite.min_quiet_ms()` is `Math.max(1000, turn_wait_ms ?? 2500)` and `turn_wait_ms` defaults to 2500 (`Recite.js:45`). Yet the readme intro (`audio/Recite/readme.md:3`) and `echo-and-turn-taking.md` both headline "at least a second". The Turn-taking settings paragraph gives the right number, so only the headline wording misleads.

The start grace applies to every chunk, which means every sentence, not just the start of each reply. `Recite.play()` calls `barge.chunk_started()` for each one (`Recite.js:209`), so the fast volume cut is blocked for the first second of every sentence. That may be intended, but neither the readme nor the doc says so.

Stale doc line: `ux/Dictate/doc/echo-and-turn-taking.md` ("Interrupts, built", Open) says the own-mic `hear()` trigger "still only fires while Recite is 'playing'". The diff changed it to fire on "playing" or "loading" (`BargeIn.js:154`). The real open gap is the held (`wait_at`) case only.

`core/Plugin/readme.md` says `Plugin.test.mjs` has "19 tests", but the file on `worktree/qf-1` has 20. Also, `Plugin.js:1-4`'s header summary still lists only the class-level API and doesn't mention `inst.plugins` / `toggle_plugin`.

Show the class: no page shows an instance's own plugin rows (`inst.plugins`). `core/Plugin/page.js` only shows `Host.plugins`, so the owner can't watch a per-instance switch live. This is already recorded as open in `requirements-qf1.md` item 3; it's fine as groundwork, but it should get a row once `mastermind-chat-settings`' panel lands.

Replaces the pause cue's reply-now prompt.
